<!--
  prd — product requirements document / product brief: what a product or feature must do.
  Lives at: `product/prds/<kebab-name>.md` (or alongside the feature it specifies).
  Authorship: canonical. SLO: 180d.
  Owner: fixed to `product`, do not substitute.
  Discipline: PROBLEM-AND-EVIDENCE BEFORE SOLUTION — success metrics sit ahead of requirements so the
    "what" is written against a measurable target; state requirements with priority so trade-offs can be
    made under pressure; a PRD is a LIVING document, not a frozen contract — revisit assumptions and open
    questions as work proceeds.
  Source: Atlassian/Confluence PRD template (primary); Marty Cagan four-elements; Lenny Rachitsky lean PRD.
  Variants: the lean variant / product brief is a strict SUBSET in DEPTH, not in section set —
    write less under each header, never fewer headers. This template's Disposition keeps every
    one; an inapplicable section reads "None.".
  Columns: Open questions — Question | Owner | Resume condition.
  Extra frontmatter: `status` (draft | in-review | approved) — a typed field rather than a `## Metadata`
    bullet, so lint, the index and a cross-type query can all tell an approved PRD from a stale draft.
  Disposition: keep every header; "None." when empty.
  Substitute: {{TITLE}} {{DATE}} {{CONFIDENCE}} {{ORIGINATION}} {{STATUS}}.
-->

## Problem statement

<!-- The user or business problem — the core pain being addressed. State the problem before any solution. Open with the page's lead sentence — see [[_authoring:wiki-authoring-spec#lead-sentence]]. -->

## Metadata

<!-- As a bullet list: author (the accountable person — not the frontmatter `owner`, which names a sub-wiki function), target release, and core team with roles. The product or feature name is the page `title`; do not restate it. Status is the `status:` frontmatter field, not a bullet here. -->

## Why now / evidence

<!-- Why this is a real problem worth solving now, backed by research, data, or customer signal. -->

## Objective & goals

<!-- Why the work exists and how it ladders up to org strategy. -->

## Target audience / users

<!-- Personas, segments, and stakeholders. Link [[domain:personas/<slug>]] or [[personas/<slug>]], and [[domain:<path>]]. -->

## Success metrics

<!-- The metrics by which success will be judged. Sits ahead of requirements so the "what" targets a measurable outcome. -->

## Assumptions

<!-- Beliefs about users, technical constraints, and business goals — revisited as the work proceeds. -->

## Requirements / solution

<!-- The "what": user stories, functional and non-functional requirements, each with a priority. Not the implementation "how". This page holds what spans a module or a release; a requirement or quality attribute bounded to one
capability lives on that `feature` instead, and a design `ui-surface` links this page rather than
restating the requirements it implements. Requirements about how well the product must work — speed,
availability, security, accessibility, often called non-functional requirements — are split between
the feature, the module and the system; the product README draws those lines. -->

## Out of scope

<!-- Explicit exclusions to prevent scope creep. -->

## Dependencies & risks

<!-- Cross-team dependencies; risks and mitigations. High-priority risks are tracked in the governance risk register, which cites this PRD — the reference runs that way, because `product/` may not cite `governance/` under the layer order. -->

## Timeline / milestones

<!-- Rough timing (per Cagan), not a fixed schedule. The date a thing ships is PARTITIONED, not owned: this page carries ROUGH TIMING only. The others are a `roadmap` commitment, a `prd`'s rough timing, a `gtm-plan`'s launch phasing, a `campaign`'s own deadlines, a `pr-faq`'s dated-to date, and a `release-notes` shipped fact — six facts, not six copies of one. See [[_authoring:wiki-fact-ownership#fact-ownership]]. -->

## Open questions

<!-- Unresolved items. One ROW each: what is open, who settles it, and the observable state that
     says it is time to settle it. "None." when nothing is open. -->

| Question | Owner | Resume condition |
|---|---|---|
| <what is unresolved> | | |
